title: Place fact
description: One record: one short fact about one place (a country, region, city, town, village or feature), written as one sentence in our own words, with the source link. Historical, fun, popular, record-breaking (`unbelievable`) or little-known. We never copy article text: `text` is a templated or rewritten sentence; the only exception is a short share-alike hook (`text_origin: source_hook`), which is kept apart, attributed and never sent to a model (`llm_ok: false`). Voyager use: the place facts section (and Places to see, the itinerary).

place.description: The place the fact is about. At least one key: `geonames_id` (the primary join key), `wikidata_qid`, `country` (country-level facts) or `link_candidates` (a hook not yet resolved; served only once a Wikidata place resolves it).

geonames_id.description: GeoNames id of the place (from Wikidata P1566, or the source's own GeoNames link).

wikidata_qid.description: Wikidata item id of the place.

admin_level.description: What kind of place it is, when the source makes it clear.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the place's country (the country itself for country-level facts).

name.description: The place's name as the source gives it.

native_id.description: The source's own id of the place, as `<scheme>:<id>` (e.g. `gnis:1234`, `factbook:gm`).

sitelinks.description: Wikidata facts only: the place's Wikipedia articles in the hook languages, used to resolve hooks to this place.

items.description: `<site>:<title>` of an article the hook links (bold links first).

link_candidates.description: Hook facts only: the articles the hook links, in order. The first one that is a Wikidata place's sitelink is the place.

fact_type.description: `historical`: founding, former names, events, heritage designation. `popular`: nicknames, mottos, symbols, well-known figures (population, area). `unbelievable`: records and superlatives (highest, lowest, oldest, largest). `little_known`: name origins, twin towns, borders, curiosities. `fun`: editorial curiosities and hooks.

text.description: The fact: one sentence in our own words, in `lang` (a short share-alike hook only when `text_origin` is `source_hook`).

text_en.description: Optional English translation made at ingest (always machine-translated).

text_origin.description: `templated`: built from typed fields with our own sentence template. `rewritten`: our own rewrite of a sentence of the source. `source_hook`: a short hook kept as the source wrote it (share-alike only; never merged, never sent to a model).

llm_ok.description: Whether the text may be given to a model (false for share-alike text and AI-reserved sources).

date_ref.description: The year, month or day the fact refers to (`1244`, `1806-10-27`; a leading `-` for BCE), for "on this day" and timelines.

value.description: The figure as the structured source gives it.

rank_scope.description: What a record is a record of (e.g. `highest point of Germany`).

quantity.description: The figure behind a record or statistic (structured sources only).

source_field.description: The source field the fact comes from (`wikidata:P571`, `factbook:Geography/Elevation/highest point`, `dyk`, `otd`, `unusual`).

name.description: Name of the work (e.g. "Wikidata", "The World Factbook (factbook.json)").

sourced.description: Whether the source cites its own sources for this fact (Wikidata: the statement has references).

source.description: The work the fact comes from (the API adds the source id and class from the source registry).

attribution.description: Attribution text to show with the fact.

licence.description: Licence of the fact. Share-alike text is never merged into our own wording or sent to a model.

confidence.description: `structured`: taken from a typed field. `extracted`: a rule or model extraction from text (`evidence_offset` kept). `corroborated`: two independent sources agree.

evidence_offset.description: For extracted facts: the character offset of the evidence span in the captured text.

ai_bot_blocked.description: True when the source's robots.txt blocks AI bots: only a title and link may be shown, never extracted text.

source_url.description: Deep link to the fact at the source (a Wikidata statement, a Wikipedia article or hook page, a Factbook country file).

as_of.description: Crawl date, the source's edit date or a frozen edition's date (CIA World Factbook: 2026-02-04), YYYY-MM-DD.

items.description: A verbatim quote from the page.

evidence.description: Up to 3 short verbatim quotes from the page that support the fact (extracted facts).
